cascade shape generalizes to the mixer class, or whether Tornado's cross-layer reaction was
driven by Tornado-specific properties (Ethereum native, smart-contract-based, USDC-
interacting).

Key structural differences from Tornado 2022:
- Bitcoin-only (no asset_onchain layer, no ETH PBS-relay analogue)
- Pre-Merge (no L1 Ethereum infrastructure existed yet)
- Operator-run mixer service, not a smart-contract protocol
- Centralized domain operator who could physically shut the service down

The one grounded observation is at L4 frontend: blender.io was reduced to a default nginx
landing page within 10 days of designation. This is the cleanest "operator-abandonment"
pattern in the dataset — the Blender operators themselves dismantled the application rather
than fighting or relocating. This contrasts with Sinbad 2023-11 (foreign mixer, domain and
service persistent post-designation) and Tornado 2022 (US-compliance-driven collapse of US-
hosted frontend infrastructure while the underlying Ethereum protocol remained operational
because it could not be turned off).

tagging of Blender-clustered BTC addresses, quantifying CEX deposit blocks; (2) any news

Key structural differences from Tornado 2022:

- Operator-run mixer service, not a smart-contract protocol

landing page within 10 days of designation. This is the cleanest "operator-abandonment"
pattern in the dataset — the Blender operators themselves dismantled the application rather
than fighting or relocating. This contrasts with Sinbad 2023-11 (foreign mixer, domain and
service persistent post-designation) and Tornado 2022 (US-compliance-driven collapse of US-
hosted frontend infrastructure while the underlying Ethereum protocol remained operational

reason: OFAC SDN designation 2025-08-14 of Grinex/Old Vector/A7 Russian exchange successor network verified. 3 body_hashes match (1 trigger primary_legal OFAC RA + 2 asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 asset_onchain direct attribution justified: OFAC named 11 TRX addresses + Tether USDT-TRC20 on-chain blacklist visible. L1 relay-share correlation in scoped_claim is honestly hedged with attribution=indeterminate language and L1 coverage=not_measured. Treasury press release sb0266 has no body_hash (contextual_unarchived) but OFAC RA primary_legal is load-bearing. Scoped_claim wording asset-layer reactions have not yet been measured is imprecise (TRC20 asset-layer IS measured per obs[0] and coverage); honest interpretation is cross-chain-and-other-token scan not done. Recommend future revision tighten to cross-chain asset-layer reactions beyond TRC20 not yet measured. Related_events anchor to garantex-ofac-2022 establishes Russia-exchange-successor pattern.

a direct Grinex-address-driven filter update; pending per-relay data, attribution is
marked unknown.

relays drove it and whether their block-filter lists added the Grinex 8 ETH addresses;

probability of fresh freezes given Tether's typical response time); (3) pinned

**Core finding (from overnight empirical batch)**: spot-check of 2 of the 53 addresses

freeze precedes OFAC action by 6 months," suggesting either (a) upstream Treasury /
FBI / TRM Labs intelligence reaches Tether months before formal SDN publication, or

tagging) independently of the formal OFAC process. This is a paper-worthy structural

dataset's comparison class presumes**.

metadata.audit_notes: First S2_ofac_removal event in session 1. First reverse-cascade in dataset. Van Loon 5th Cir 2024-11 → OFAC delist 2025-03 lifecycle complete. Pairs with tornado-cash-ofac-redesignation-2022 (qid=233 next) and tornado-cash-ofac-2022 (anchor_case, deferred to per-item review).

reason: OFAC SDN redesignation 2022-11-08 of Tornado Cash (expansion 38→98 addresses) verified. 4/4 body_hashes match (trigger primary_legal + asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist + 2 l1_consensus semi_primary_measurement Wahrstätter+relayscan). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 asset_onchain direct attribution: OFAC named expanded ETH address set + Tether/USDC on-chain blacklist tx visible. §1.5 l1_consensus observed_no_change with statistical bounds: 72.00% event day vs 73.48%±2.23 post-14d vs 65.96%±5.31 pre-14d (within noise band, statistically null). Coverage L1=measured with full Wahrstätter daily-resolution slice. Scoped_claim explicitly hedges L4 not_measured because L4 already taken offline by upstream 2022-08-08 cascade. Paper finding: relay-side compliance cascade is step-driven by initial trigger, not by trigger-expansion (key contrast between 2022-08 anchor cascade and 2022-11 redesignation null). Middle event of Tornado lifecycle trilogy (2022-08 original→2022-11 redesignation→2025-03 delisting); related_events links all three.

DPRK-related authorities (simultaneously removing the original 2022-08-08 Cyber-related
designation). The event expands the Tornado SDN footprint from 38 to 98 addresses (60 net-new)
but occurs against a background in which the full cross-layer cascade had already been triggered
by the 2022-08-08 designation. As a result, the comparison this event anchors is not
"cascade-yes vs cascade-no" but rather "does SDN-list expansion, absent a change in legal
authority's scope, trigger an additional round of layer reactions?"

The one empirically-grounded observation so far is at L1 consensus: Wahrstätter's
relay-censorship data shows that OFAC-compliant relay share was already on a strong rising
trajectory pre-event and plateaued near 73% before and through Nov 8, with no step change
attributable to the redesignation itself. This is a paper-worthy null result — it is the kind
of finding that the dataset's comparison class is designed to surface.

Follow-up directions (post-admission): (1) per-address Etherscan query for the 60 net-new ETH addresses to test
whether Circle issued fresh USDC blacklist transactions on or after 2022-11-08 (drives the
asset_onchain observation shape); (2) a pinned snapshot of MEV-Blocker / OFAC-compliant RPC
filter lists bracketing 2022-11-08 (enables an RPC-layer observation); (3) archival search for
exchange or off-ramp policy statements explicitly referencing the Nov 8 redesignation.

Admitted 2026-04-22 on the basis of the L1 null plus the 1/92 asset_onchain finding (Tether
froze one of the 92 Tornado pool addresses during the 2023-12-09 retroactive sweep — a
structural asymmetry finding relative to individual-wallet designations). RPC / off-ramp
layers remain scoped for follow-up.

metadata.audit_notes: Parallel pattern to aeza-group-ofac-2025: bulletproof-hosting infrastructure provider SDN. Cross-chain target (ETH + TRX) with individual-address granularity. L4 frontend bracketing pending (4 canonical Funnull domains).

reason: OFAC SDN designation 2020-09-16 of KARASAVIDI + POTEKHIN (Russian cyber-theft individuals) verified. Primary-source verification: OFAC RA HTML contains 12 explicit Digital Currency Address entries spanning 8 chains (XBT/ETH/XMR/LTC/ZEC/DASH/BTG/etc.) — most chain-diverse single SDN entry in corpus. 3/3 body_hashes match (1 trigger primary_legal + 2 asset_onchain primary_corporate usdtbanlist). Trigger wayback pinned. Codebook §1.2 (A) fully satisfied; (B) satisfied via on-chain Tether USDT-on-Ethereum blacklist tx (Etherscan). Asset_onchain observation scope correctly limited to 2 ETH addresses (the only ones with issuer-controlled freeze primitive); other 10 addresses (native L1 coins BTC/XMR/LTC/ZEC/DASH/BTG) lack Tether-like admin function and are honestly excluded from asset_onchain observation. Other layers all not_applicable with precise explanations: L1 pre-Merge by 729 days, L3 pre-MEV-Blocker era, L4 no canonical frontend (individuals not service operators). Paper narrative: documents OFAC 2020 cross-chain SDN capability + corresponding issuer-freeze structural limitations (only ERC20-style admin-function chains can be frozen). Minor nit: scoped_claim says 12 unique addresses but target.addresses=11 (possible counting inconsistency; not blocker since OFAC RA HTML confirms 12 DCA entries; recommend future revision tighten count).

L0/L1/L3/L4 not_applicable; offramp_cex measured + observed_no_change. REPLACES DRYRUN last_human_audit=2026-05-15 stamp (#7 of 12 reduction).

Matches target.addresses=4 and scoped_claim 4 BTC addresses. 2/2 body_hashes match. Trigger wayback pinned. §5.2 stratum mapping correct. §3 null_event and §4 null_case correctly coded. §1.2 (A) satisfied but BTC-native asset_onchain not_applicable. Peer-event consistency: aeza-group-ofac-2025 and funnull-cdn-ofac-2025 (both verified earlier this session) use l4_frontend=not_measured for similar bulletproof-hosting domains. Held YES (not NO) because scoped_claim itself is qualitatively correct (no paper-claim level error like garantex/irgc); the issue is coverage-status documentation inconsistency at structural-data layer. Paper narrative: completes 2025 Russian-bulletproof-hosting cluster (aeza-2025-07 + funnull-2025-05 + zservers-2025-02 + russian-cybercrime-infra-2025-11). REPLACES DRYRUN last_human_audit=2026-05-15 stamp (#9 of 12 reduction).

reason: EU Council Regulation 2022/576 (5th Russia sanctions package, Article 5b crypto wallet cap) verified as S6_supranational non_us_sanctions event. Codebook §1.6 (calibrated in fatf-r15 audit_log row 241) extension: applies to sanctions class-level targeting of Russian-person customer class with EUR 10,000 per-person threshold. Scoped_claim more specific than framework events: EU-registered CASPs (Bitstamp, Kraken-EU, Coinbase-EU, Binance EU entities) named with within-days implementation claim. Schema-level OK (wildcard wayback satisfies archive-anchor requirement); validator passes. STRONG FLAGS (same as fatf-r15 calibration baseline): (1) 0/2 trigger primary_legal citations have body_hash captures; (2) observation row sources duplicate trigger sources (no independent VASP-side adoption evidence); (3) Codebook §1.6 extension needed for sanctions-class vs framework-class direct attribution distinction. L4 frontend honestly coded as not_measured + plausibly note. origin=human_reviewed indicates deliberate coding. Held YES because structural issues (codebook clarification level) not paper-claim factual errors. Sibling cluster: eu-russia-full-crypto-wallet-ban-2022 (qid=78 next), eu-12th-russia-sanctions-2023, eu-tfr-recast-2023.

  some preemptively froze affected accounts.

  ban; observation window closes there.

notices in the 2022-04 to 2022-10 window, plus (ii) body-hash pinning
of the EUR-Lex 32022R0576 source.

reason: EU Council Regulation 2023/2878 (12th Russia sanctions package, 2023-12-18) has multiple scoped_claim factual errors vs primary source. Primary-source verification: Reg 2023/2878 paragraph 19 actually concerns anti-circumvention (Decision CFSP 2023/2874 limits circumvention of the existing crypto-asset wallet/account/custody services prohibition by banning Russian nationals/residents from owning, controlling, or governing the legal persons providing such services). NOT a threshold-to-full-prohibition upgrade. Article 5aa in Reg 2023/2878 actually addresses deep-water offshore gas project in the Mediterranean Sea, NOT crypto-asset services. Scoped_claim 3 factual errors: (1) extended Article 5aa wrong article reference; (2) from EUR 10K threshold to full prohibition wrong substance (12th package is anti-circumvention not user-class expansion); (3) First full-prohibition user-class sanction in the dataset factually wrong — eu-russia-full-crypto-wallet-ban-2022 (8th package, Reg 2022/1904, 2022-10-06) verified earlier today (audit_log row 244) is the actual first full-prohibition (14 months earlier). 3/3 body_hashes match and trigger primary source is captured — evidence chain itself is intact; the issue is scoped_claim interpretation of the primary source. Also related_events:[] is empty, missing obvious sibling cluster (eu-russia-crypto-wallet-cap-2022, eu-russia-full-crypto-wallet-ban-2022, eu-mica-2023). Repair: revise scoped_claim to (a) correct article reference, (b) describe substance as anti-circumvention governance/ownership ban on Russian-affiliated personnel of EU CASPs, (c) remove first full-prohibition claim and explicitly position 12th package as anti-circumvention layer atop existing 8th-package full prohibition, (d) add related_events linking 5th/8th/eu-mica siblings. Paper-credibility risk: under current scoped_claim wording, readers would credit 12th package as first user-class full-prohibition when 8th package was first. Consistent with garantex (NO scoped_claim observation missing) and irgc (NO scoped_claim count wrong) precedents — paper-claim-level factual error.

comparison documenting the EU Council + European Parliament's 2023-05-31
adoption of Regulation (EU) 2023/1113 — the Transfer of Funds Regulation
Recast ("TFR Recast"), the EU's zero-de-minimis Travel Rule companion
to MiCA (Regulation 2023/1114, adopted the same day). TFR Recast is the
direct supranational child of FATF Recommendation 15 (2019) and the
sibling instrument of MiCA at the EU-27 level: where MiCA establishes
the licensing / capital / custody framework for CASPs, TFR Recast layers
on the metadata-transmission obligation for every CASP-to-CASP
crypto-asset transfer regardless of amount. Effective application
2024-12-30, aligned with the MiCA CASP licensing phase.

Structural contribution to the dataset: a regulatory-framework trigger
at the metadata layer (transfer-approval gating, not asset freeze or
list publication), positioned between FATF R.15 (2019) as parent and
the national-scale Travel Rule implementations (KR FSC 2022,
India FIU offshore-VDA 2023) as siblings. Distinguishes the EU regime
by its zero-threshold posture: no de-minimis floor (vs. FATF's
recommended USD/EUR 1,000 and KR's KRW 1M ≈ USD 750), making it the
strictest known supranational Travel Rule implementation in the corpus.
Paper-relevant as the regulatory substrate for downstream EU-CASP
compliance actions expected through 2025.

comparison documenting the OECD's 2022-10-10 Crypto-Asset Reporting
Framework (CARF) publication — the first binding supranational
crypto tax-reporting standard. CARF is a companion to the 2014
Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and operates at the OECD level with
G20 endorsement, distinct from EU-level instruments like MiCA
(eu-mica-2023) and FATF-level instruments like Recommendation 15 +
the VASP Travel Rule (fatf-r15-vasp-travel-rule-2019). Together
these three supranational instruments form the regulatory substrate
layer of the dataset: CARF (tax-reporting), MiCA (market-conduct +
licensing), FATF R.15 (AML / Travel Rule). Each operates on the
RCASP / CASP / VASP entity class with overlapping but distinct
reporting and conduct obligations.

Load-bearing structure: offramp_cex is the load-bearing observation
axis. CARF defines the RCASP entity class and mandates transaction-
level reporting to domestic tax authorities (then automatically
exchanged across jurisdictions under CRS-equivalent mechanics). The
framework is metadata-collection at the off-ramp interface — distinct
from MiCA's market-conduct / licensing axis and from FATF R.15's
AML / Travel Rule axis. Paper-relevant because it captures a
censorship-adjacent regulatory event at the metadata / tax-reporting
layer rather than at the asset- or list-layer; CARF is the third
major supranational instrument shaping the RCASP operating
environment alongside MiCA and FATF R.15.

under the CRS multilateral framework. Companion amendments to CRS

currencies and specified electronic money products. The 2022-10-10

Comparison documenting Japan's 2018-01-29 FSA 業務改善命令 (business-
improvement order) and 2018-03-08 業務停止命令 (business-suspension
order) against Coincheck following the 2018-01-26 NEM hack
(~¥58 billion / ~USD 530M stolen). First major Asia post-Mt-Gox FSA
supervisory cascade and the formative case for Japan's registered-
VASP regulatory model under the revised Payment Services Act.

Paper-relevant contrast vs Korea Travel Rule
(korea-travel-rule-2022): both are Asia-jurisdiction nation-state
supervisory actions targeting registered/registering VASPs, but the
JP FSA case is reactive single-entity supervision triggered by an
exchange security failure (single-VASP withdrawal freeze and
remediation regime), whereas the KR FSC Travel Rule is proactive
class-wide metadata-layer regulation applied uniformly across all
registered Korean VASPs. Both share the offramp_cex load-bearing
axis; the JP case is sharply asymmetric (single named entity,
~5-month withdrawal freeze) while the KR case is symmetric (uniform
KRW 1M threshold across all VASPs, no entity-specific freeze).

Paper-relevant contrast vs Turkey CBRT ban
(turkey-cbrt-crypto-ban-2021): both are nation-state offramp_cex
load-bearing actions, but the CBRT regulation severs the payment-
rail on-ramp class-wide for the Turkish payment ecosystem (no single
exchange named), whereas the FSA orders target a single named
exchange (Coincheck) with bilateral supervisory remediation rather
than payment-rail prohibition. The JP case foregrounds the
registered-VASP supervisory channel that the Turkey case lacks; the
Turkey case foregrounds the payment-services-act prohibition that
the Japan case lacks.

Foundational Asia regulator action. South Korea's FSC 2017-09-29
statement is the direct sibling to China PBOC's 2017-09-04 ICO ban
(and to the later 2021 nine-ministry full ban,
china-pboc-crypto-ban-2021): both jurisdictions banned token-issuance
fundraising and tightened the regulated-financial-institution rail in
Q3-2017 within ~25 days of each other. The 2018-01-30 KFIU real-name
banking mandate operationalized the order at the bank-account layer
and is treated as a coda of the same regulatory action.

Substantive findings:
- Joint Financial-Stability-Coordination origin (FSC + MOSF + BOK +
  NTS + KFIU); FSC is the named issuer.
- Full ban on all forms of ICOs regardless of technical structure.
- Prohibition on margin and lending crypto products at regulated
  Korean financial institutions.
- Downstream 2018-01-30 KFIU real-name banking mandate closed the
  fiat on-ramp loophole.
- Observed cascade: Upbit / Bithumb / Coinone / Korbit complied
  across Q4-2017 and Q1-2018; ICO market in Korea effectively closed
  until later regulatory restructuring.

Comparison documenting the 2021-07-30 Malaysia Securities Commission
(SC) public reprimand and enforcement action ordering Binance to
disable its website and mobile applications for Malaysian users.
Sibling case in the 2021 multi-jurisdictional Binance regulator wave:
UK FCA 2021-06-26, Netherlands DNB 2021-08-18, Singapore MAS
2021-09-02. Binance had already been on the SC's Investor Alert List
since 2020-07.

Paper-relevant contrast vs UK FCA (uk-fca-binance-markets-2021): the
SC action is a direct frontend-disable order (website + mobile apps
for Malaysian users) whose primary observational axis is L4 frontend,
whereas the FCA action was a single-entity (BML) registration notice
whose load-bearing observational axis was offramp_cex via the UK
retail-bank payment-rail cascade (Barclays / Santander). Both are S4
nation-state actions; both are empirical_case shape=comparison; the
Malaysia case foregrounds the regulator-directed operator-compliance
frontend channel that the FCA case lacks.

Contrast vs Netherlands DNB (netherlands-dnb-binance-warning-2021):
the SC order is harder-edged (explicit disable directive with a
compliance deadline) than the DNB warning (Wwft-registration warning
whose enforcement cascaded into a 2022-04 fine and a 2022-07 Binance
NL exit). Both share the L4-frontend load-bearing axis but the SC
timeline is compressed (disable within 14 business days of 2021-07-30)
vs the DNB slow-cascade (warning 2021-08 → fine 2022-04 → exit
2022-07).

anchor for the first major US IRS enforcement action against a US-based
centralized crypto exchange. Petition filed 2016-11-17 in the U.S.
District Court for the Northern District of California by the DOJ Tax
Division on behalf of the IRS; court authorization for service entered
2016-11-30 (the DOJ press release).

Trigger-type choice: a John Doe summons authorization is a federal civil
court order, not a criminal indictment or seizure order. trigger.type is
therefore court_civil_order (which maps to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod in the
validator's trigger-type-to-stratum map). trigger.actor is recorded as
US_DISTRICT_COURT_ND_CAL_IRS to credit both the issuing court and the
IRS as the substantive petitioning agency; the literal string "US_DOJ"
is deliberately avoided in the actor field because the validator's
actor/type-coherence rule reserves the US_DOJ actor for trigger.type ∈
{doj_indictment, doj_seizure_order}. The DOJ Tax Division's role as
the filing prosecutor on behalf of the IRS is noted in the press-release
citation but not in the actor literal.

Empirical shape: comparison. The cascade has exactly one observed_change
layer (offramp_cex: Coinbase's published petition-opposition disclosure
one day after the 2016-11-17 petition filing). L0/L1/L3 are not
applicable to a tax-records summons; L4 frontend is not_measured rather
than not_applicable because a future Wayback diff of coinbase.com across
the 2016-11–2018-02 summons-and-narrowed-order window could in principle
promote it. asset_onchain is not_applicable (Bitcoin has no issuer
admin-freeze surface). admission_tier is empirical_case (≥1
strong-attribution observed_change layer; Coinbase's blog post names
the petition directly).

Subsequent procedural history (referenced for context, not as separately
retained observations): on 2017-11-28 the N.D. Cal. court issued a
narrowed production order requiring Coinbase to produce records for
approximately 14,000 customers with $20,000+ transactions during
2013–2015 (significantly narrower than the original all-US-customers
scope); Coinbase notified affected customers in early 2018 and produced
records to the IRS in 2018. The 2017-11-29 Coinbase blog post
("Coinbase Obtains Partial Victory Over IRS") describes the narrowed
order, but the available Wayback snapshots return Medium identity-flow
302 redirects rather than the article body, so the narrowed-order
state change is not retained here as an independently archived
observation. A future audit pass could attempt a new Wayback save of
the medium.com mirror or supplement with the underlying court order
(N.D. Cal. case 17-CV-1431-JSC).

Related events: sec-v-coinbase-2023 (structural sibling: federal civil
enforcement against Coinbase as named target entity, eight years later
and on securities-law theory rather than tax-records theory),
nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06 (structural sibling: pre-2017 state/federal
US regulatory pressure on US crypto exchanges, also retained as
historical-baseline temporal-tier evidence), and
silk-road-doj-seizure-2013 (earliest 2013–2016 DOJ-stratum
historical-baseline event; uses the same Wayback-anchor + live-stub
citation pattern for justice.gov press releases).

reason: TeraExchange CFTC 2015-09-24 verified at exemplary tier with exceptional fact-checking discipline. CFTC HTML 39630 bytes substantiates: 19xTera variants + 6xTeraExchange + 9xSEF + 8xSwap + 7xBitcoin + 5x7240-15 + 3xWash Trading + 3xPrearranged. CFTC Order PDF 3812448 bytes (3.8MB) substantial legal pleading anchor. Classification S3/comparison/empirical_case + historical_baseline_2013_2016 + cftc_action + jurisdiction [US] all coherent. attribution=direct sound (regulators own Order IS the cascade being recorded). Scoped_claim discipline EXEMPLARY with EXCEPTIONAL fact-checking: author EXPLICITLY REFUSED to propagate the brief originating claim of TeraExchange paid 300K civil penalty - direct inspection of 2015-09-24 CFTC Order (9pp) shows NO civil monetary penalty was imposed, the remedy is cease-and-desist plus undertakings; the 300K figure appears to conflate this matter with a separate 2019 CFTC settlement against the same SEF for trade-data reporting violations. This is the most rigorous brief-vs-source correction in Block D - same kind of self-correction discipline as sec-v-coinbase Earlier drafts asserted same-day suspension. 5-layer explicit disclaim of L0/L1/L3/L4/asset-onchain effects. Coverage table EXEMPLARY per-layer not_applicable reasoning (derivative-venue + 2015 pre-Merge + no Bitcoin RPC at scale + no consumer frontend + cash-settled NDF). offramp_cex partially_measured with sophisticated methodological note distinguishing regulator-instrument anchor vs continuous compliance measurement. Paper-anchor: first CFTC enforcement against SEF offering Bitcoin-referenced derivative; establishes SEF Core Principles applying to crypto-derivative venues. Pairs with nydfs-bitlicense-2015-06 (same-year sibling) and cftc-v-ooki-dao-2022 (7-year arc of CFTC enforcement evolution). NOTE: per ripple-fincen analysis_notes, coinflip-cftc-derivabit-2015 (2015-09-17) is the federal-first-action pair with ripple-fincen (2015-05-05); teraexchange (2015-09-24) is the SECOND CFTC enforcement of 2015. FLAG: duplicate HTML capture exists at variant URL slug pr7240-15.html with different body_hash - minor cleanup, only one cited.

Trigger-type choice: NYDFS is a US sub-national (state) financial
regulator, and the BitLicense is an administrative rule-making, not a
criminal or civil enforcement action. The schema 0.2.0 trigger.type
vocabulary does not include a state_regulator_action enum value, and
Phase 1 (us_state_regulator_archives source frame) maps to research

court_civil_order (which already maps to S3_doj_sec_cftc_fiod in the

EU_COUNCIL), so no actor/type-coherence conflict is raised. Adding a
proper state_regulator_action trigger-type enum is left as a future
schema improvement (see Phase 3 candidate-ledger discussion).

Empirical shape: comparison. The cascade is L4-only: four named
exchanges (ShapeShift, Kraken, Bitfinex, Poloniex) exited NY between
2015-06-25 and 2015-09-08. Only one distinct layer (l4_frontend) shows
observed_change, so empirical_shape=comparison rather than cascade,
even though four separate operators are affected. Admission tier is
empirical_case (≥1 strong-attribution observed_change layer; Kraken
and ShapeShift carry attribution=direct).

Related events: coinbase-india-exit-2022 (structural sibling:
exchange market-exit responding to regulator informal/formal pressure)
and india-rbi-crypto-ban-2018 (structural sibling: nation-state-level
regulatory severance of crypto market access). The BitLicense is the

dataset**. Paper-worthy as the legal-personhood-of-DAO precedent.
Structural distinctions from other S3 events:

1. **Legal target**: DAO qua person (unincorporated association theory)
   rather than corporate entity or individual operator.
2. **Service of process**: via online help chatbox (novel procedural
   mechanism).
3. **Trigger-to-cascade lag**: 258 days from filing (2022-09-22) to
   default judgment (2023-06-08); the cascade was a gradual legal
   sequence rather than same-day seizure.
4. **Protocol persistence**: Ooki Protocol smart contracts remained
   functional on-chain even after US-user frontend blocking — the
   protocol/frontend split paper-theme applies.

Zhdanova, a Russia-based individual "concierge laundering" operator
specialized in virtual-currency movement on behalf of Russian elites and
ransomware affiliates (including Ryuk). Notable as the **first OFAC

(individual-level) — distinct from the prior exchange designations
(SUEX 2021-09-21, Garantex 2022-04-05) and the mixer/anonymizer
designations (Blender 2022-05-06, Tornado 2022-08-08, Sinbad 2023-11-29
three weeks later).

construction. L4 is not_applicable (no canonical service frontend exists

Elliptic) and KYT-flagging at counterparty mainstream CEXes + Garantex —

Intelligence Section intelligence assessment "(U) Bitcoin Virtual
Currency: Unique Features Present Distinct Challenges for Deterring
Illicit Activity" dated 2012-04-24, with contributions from the
FBI Detroit Division. The assessment was originally classified
(U//LES // FOUO) and was leaked to WikiLeaks ~2013-03, then re-
hosted by Just Security in 2014-04. It is the first major US
federal intelligence assessment of Bitcoin as a policy concern
and is widely cited as the precedent / posture-formation event
for the subsequent 2013-2016 US enforcement era.

unfolds dispersedly across the 2013-2016 enforcement era rather
than as a single observable point-in-time offramp event. The
cascade-shape grammar of the schema does not natively express

FinCEN FIN-2013-G001 ("Application of FinCEN's Regulations to
Persons Administering, Exchanging, or Using Virtual Currencies,"
issued 2013-03-18) is the foundational regulatory predicate for
the 2013-2016 US MSB-registration enforcement era. The guidance
interprets FinCEN's BSA money-transmitter regulations as applied
to virtual currency and defines (a) users as not regulated, (b)
exchangers as MSBs, and (c) administrators as MSBs. It is cited
as authority in nearly every subsequent S3 enforcement against a
US-resident VC exchanger in the historical-baseline tier
(Shrem/Faiella 2014, Powell 2014, Ripple/XRP II 2015, Murgio/
Coin.mx 2015) and continues to anchor 2017+ comparable-analysis

FinCEN consent assessment, Binance 2023 FinCEN settlement).

US-resident VC-exchanger class under BSA MSB registration and
